descriptions.text: According to Yonhap News Agency, Kim Seok-hwan, a representative of Wemix Foundation, a blockchain subsidiary of Wemade, admitted at an emergency meeting that they lost approximately 8.65 million WEMIX tokens (worth about $6.22 million) due to a hack. On February 28, the hacker stole the authentication key of the NFT platform "Nile" and attacked the Play Bridge Vault system.

On 28 February 2025, attackers used a stolen authentication key for Wemix's Nile platform to conduct 13 unauthorized withdrawals totaling 8,654,860 WEMIX tokens (approximately $6.22 million). The breach originated from a shared repository exposure, bypassing application and on-chain controls. Funds were rapidly dispersed via exchanges. There is no public evidence of recovered assets or forensic follow-up. The principal cause was a developer's inadvertent upload of privileged authentication keys for the Nile platform's monitoring service to a shared repository, exposing them for months. Attackers subsequently obtained the key and used it to bypass withdrawal controls.…
